note: CRIF Jordan's own page 'Retaining and displaying data on the credit report', read from archive.org's snapshot of 16 January 2025 (crif.jo's live pages were read earlier and gave only the cheque periods; a later version of this page wasn't found among the archive's captures). It states the periods 'as specified by the regulatory authority's instructions' (the Central Bank of Jordan's; the instructions themselves weren't read): data on late payments stays visible for three years from the repayment of each instalment or the clearance of the customer's liability. The page counts only from repayment, so a late payment stays while unpaid: written as keep 30, the longest the game keeps (the convention for 'kept as long as unpaid'), lifting three years after it is paid, 1096 days (three years of 365.25 days). The same page puts a written-off debt at five years from the write-off and a final court ruling at five years from the ruling (each, or three years from clearance, whichever is earlier); the form holds one period for a late payment and these aren't used. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the next monthly update.

sources.title: CRIF Jordan: Retaining and displaying data on the credit report (archive.org snapshot of 16 January 2025)
sources.said: The periods for retaining and displaying data on the credit report as specified by the regulatory authority's instructions are: ... 2. Data related to late payments remains visible on the credit report for a period of 3 years from the date of repayment of each installment or the clearance of the customer's liability. ... 5. Data related to debt write-offs remains visible on the credit report for a period of 5 years from the date the debt was fully or partially written off, or 3 years from the date the indebtedness was paid off or the customer's liability was cleared in any form, whichever is earlier.
